scenes.vo: A candy bar melted in his pocket in 1945.
Before 1945, cooking meant fire and patience. After one strange afternoon, it meant invisible waves doing the work in minutes.
Percy Spencer felt no heat at all. The radar waves had done it.
He held popcorn near the machine. It popped. An egg exploded in a colleague's face. Microwaves cook from inside.
The Radarange was born. Six feet tall. It changed every kitchen.

caption:
Percy Spencer invented the microwave by accident in 1945

A candy bar melted in his pocket near a radar machine. Popcorn popped. An egg exploded. The Radarange was born.

Send this to whoever reheats leftovers daily.
Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KN2strNPbaE

brief.story_core: Cooking had always pushed heat in from the outside; one melted candy bar showed Percy Spencer that invisible waves could cook a thing from its own centre while the man holding it felt nothing.
brief.emotion: Curious unease (why is it melting?), then the delight of a slapstick accident (pop, splat), turning into quiet awe that a six-foot lab machine became the small box in every kitchen.
brief.hook: Frame 0: an enlarged cutaway detail circle on drafting paper, a chocolate bar inside a jacket pocket shown in section, its core already faintly hot-red. At 0.1 s a thin dashed wave front crosses the cloth from the right without touching it; the bar core flushes; by 1 s the bar sags and a drop of chocolate runs out of the section and soaks into the hatched lining. No title, no big text.
brief.visual_question: What is melting a chocolate bar inside a pocket when nothing near it is hot?
brief.metaphor: The engineering cutaway: microwaves cook from the inside, so the film only ever looks inside things, and heat is the single colour that blooms from their cores outward.
brief.world: One 1940s technical cutaway sheet on drafting paper: detail circles, phantom-lined figure of Spencer, a sectioned magnetron, a sectioned pot, kernel and egg, a Radarange with dimension lines, an apartment elevation and a title block.
brief.camera: One camera over one sheet: open inside Detail A at 6:1, travel down the sheet to the before/after sections, rise up the phantom figure to reveal the pocket was his, push into Detail B and C, take the egg on the lens, wipe it, pull far back to the building elevation and settle on the title block.
brief.motion: Physical and fluid: chocolate slumps with weight, heat blooms centre-out, the kernel shivers under pressure then ruptures with overshoot, shell shards fly with gravity, yolk slides down the glass. Long holds while heat builds, then sudden events.
brief.typography: Futura as engraved drawing labels (FIG., DETAIL A, SCALE 6:1, dimension figures 6 ft), drawn on with leader lines; the name and the year stamp in the heat colour as they are spoken; captions as italic Baskerville figure captions under each drawing.
brief.material: Theme cutaway: chocolate-brown ink on warm drafting paper, line hatching for shade and section, phantom dash lines for the man, one heat red-orange used only for waves and what they cook from inside; paper grain and a fixed ink roughness.
brief.transitions: Moves along the sheet: the detail circle leads to the next figure along its leader line; the egg splatter lands on the lens and a cloth wipe clears it into the next shot; the countertop box drops into one window of a building elevation.
brief.sound: Music-led with a dry mid-century score; foley only on physical events: a soft drip, three clock ticks for patience, the magnetron clunk, the pop, the shell crack, a wet splat on the lens, the cloth wipe, a pen drawing the dimension, a title-block stamp. Music hushes the half second before the egg goes.

music.caption: mid-century science-film cue, vibraphone and pizzicato upright bass with brushed snare and muted trumpet, curious and playful, sparse start, a gentle swing groove builds, short break, bright resolving finish

brief.payoff: The egg explodes at the viewer and splatters the lens before a cloth wipes it clean; then the six-foot Radarange shrinks into a countertop box that becomes one lit window in a whole building of kitchens.
